lessons.title: The CPS Framework
lessons.html:
Every script in this playbook uses the same structure. Learn it once and you will use it forever.

C = Compliment

Something specific you actually noticed. Not "love your page", something real that shows you looked.

P = Point out the gap

One thing that is quietly costing them clients or money. You are not criticising them. You are showing them you paid attention.

S = Solution + CTA

Ask for their WhatsApp number. Not a formal call. Not a calendar link. Just "what's your WhatsApp, I'll send you a quick voice note on this" or "drop your WhatsApp and I'll walk you through it."

Think of it as: hey, I noticed this thing, here is what it might mean, drop your WhatsApp and I'll explain.

The framework works from 7 angles. Pick the one that fits the person you are messaging. Every script ends with the same goal: get their WhatsApp number so you can have a real conversation.

lessons.title: Crafting Your Grand Slam Offer
lessons.html:
If you want people to buy from you without begging, discounting, or explaining yourself 24/7, you need an offer so good, your ideal client thinks:

“This feels like a steal… I’d be crazy to say no.”

That’s what Alex Hormozi calls a Grand Slam Offer , and don’t worry, you don’t need a business degree to make one.

Just follow this simple 5-step formula:

STEP 1:

Solve ONE clear problem

Skip the fluff. Pick one painful problem your ideal client is struggling with and promise to fix it.

Not:

“I do content, admin, and mindset coaching.”

Say:

“I help overwhelmed service providers book their first 5 clients without posting every day.”

Make it specific, clear, and valuable.

STEP 2: Add Urgency (So They ACT Now)

People procrastinate unless you give them a reason to move today.

Easy ways to add urgency:

  • “Only 3 spots available this month”
  • “Beta price ends Friday”
  • “I’m only working with 5 people at this rate”

Scarcity = action. No urgency = ghosted DMs.

STEP 3: Stack the Value

Now package your offer like this:

  1. Main solution – Your core service or product (e.g. coaching, a done-for-you system, templates, etc.)
  2. Bonuses – Little extras that make it feel like more than they expected (worksheets, templates, support group, audits, etc.)
  3. Support – Can they message you? Weekly check-ins? Private group chat?
  4. Guarantees – Risk reversal like “Cancel anytime” or “I don’t stop until you get results”

Tip: The goal is to make it feel like 10x the value of the price.

STEP 4: Charge Based on the Result Not Your Time

You’re not selling hours. You’re selling outcomes.

If your offer helps someone:

  • Save time
  • Make money
  • Fix a painful problem
  • Gain confidence

…then it’s worth way more than what you’ve been charging.

Price it like it actually works because it does.

STEP 5: Make It EASY to Say Yes

  • One clear CTA: “DM me ‘Ready’ to start”
  • Simple onboarding
  • Quick win in week 1
  • No long, confusing process

Remove all the friction.

Make it feel like buying from you = instant relief.

Recap: Your Grand Slam Offer =

✅ Solves a specific painful problem

✅ Comes with juicy bonuses + simple support

✅ Has urgency so people act now

✅ Feels like insane value for the price

✅ Is so easy to say yes to, it’s almost automatic

lessons.title: How to Find 20 Ideal Prospects in 20 Minutes
lessons.html:
Spending 3 minutes finding the right person before you send anything is what separates a 70% reply rate from a 10% one. This page shows you how to find 20 ideal prospects in 20 minutes on any platform.

The Rule

You are not looking for someone who might need you. You are looking for someone who clearly already has the problem you solve and hasn't hired anyone to fix it yet. That distinction changes everything. You're not guessing. You're observing.

On Instagram

Method 1: Hashtag Search

Search a hashtag your ideal client uses. Not a service hashtag. Their industry hashtag.

Instead of #socialmediamanager, search #esthetician or #fitnesstrainer or #graphicdesigner. Filter for recent posts. Open profiles that look like real businesses with an audience. Look for the gap.

Method 2: Competitor's Followers

Find a business in your niche that has the type of clients you want. Go to their followers list. These are people who have already shown interest in this type of service. Browse and find accounts that match who you're looking for.

Method 3: Explore Page

Search your niche keyword in Instagram Explore. Look for business accounts with decent engagement but an obvious gap in their profile or content.

On Twitter/X

Search a pain point your ideal client would actually tweet about. Things like "need a designer" or "looking for a social media manager" or "why is my content not converting." These are people actively expressing the exact problem you solve. Reply publicly first to build a little rapport, then DM.

The 5 Gap Signals to Look For

These become the P in your CPS message:

What You SeeWhat It's Costing Them
Strong content but no call to actionLosing warm traffic every day
Bio doesn't say what they sell or how to hire themVisitors leave without knowing how to become a client
Highlights not updated in 6 monthsSocial proof looks abandoned
Good engagement but link in bio goes nowhereWarm audience with no conversion path
Posts inconsistently, bursts then nothingNo system, probably managing it alone

Your 20-Minute Routine

TimeWhat to Do
Minutes 1 to 10Find 10 prospects using one method above
Minutes 11 to 15Open each profile, spot their specific gap
Minutes 16 to 20Write their gap observation in one sentence

That one sentence becomes the C and P of your CPS message. The script handles the rest.

Safe Daily Volumes

  • Instagram: 10 to 20 targeted DMs per day
  • LinkedIn: 10 to 15 connection requests or messages per day
  • Twitter/X: No hard limit, quality beats volume
  • Email: 20 to 40 personalised cold emails per day
Spend at least 2 minutes on every prospect's profile before sending. DMs that get ignored could have been sent to anyone. DMs that get replies could only have been sent to that specific person.

lessons.title: 4 AI Prompt: Fill In The Blanks Fast
lessons.html:
Use this with ChatGPT or Claude to personalise any script from this playbook in under 60 seconds. You still need to read it before sending. The AI gets you 90% there. Your eye finishes it.

How to Use This

  1. Copy the prompt below
  2. Paste it into ChatGPT or Claude
  3. Fill in the five inputs
  4. Read the output once, tweak a word or two, send

The Main Prompt

Copy this exactly and fill in your details:

Prompt
You are a cold outreach specialist who writes direct messages that sound like a real person typing, not a marketer or a template. Help me personalise one cold DM using the CPS Framework (Compliment, Point Out the Gap, Soft Ask).

My niche/service: [what you do, e.g. social media management, graphic design, video editing]

Platform I'm sending on: [Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, WhatsApp, or Email]

Something specific I noticed about them: [one real observation, e.g. their last 3 posts have no call to action, their bio doesn't say what they sell, their highlights haven't been updated in months]

What that observation is costing them: [e.g. they're losing warm traffic, prospects don't know how to hire them]

Script angle I want: [Problem-Focused / Result-Oriented / Value-Based / Compliment + Audit / Direct / Soft Question / Niche-Expertise]

Write me one cold DM based on the above. Rules:
- Maximum 4 sentences
- Sound like a real person, not a sales pitch
- Do not use: "I hope this finds you well", "I came across your profile", "I wanted to reach out", "game-changer", "elevate", "transform", "unlock"
- The compliment must be about the specific thing I noticed, not their page in general
- The gap is an observation, not a criticism
- The ask is one question they can answer in under 10 seconds
- No price, no packages, no full offer in this message
- No emojis unless I ask
- Write in first person as me

After the DM, write one sentence explaining why you worded the ask that way.

Quick Rewrite Prompt

Already have a draft and want it to sound more natural? Use this:

Prompt
Rewrite this cold DM so it sounds completely human. Keep it under 4 sentences. Remove anything that sounds like a template. Keep the observation and the ask. No emojis. Do not change the niche or the offer.

My draft: [paste your draft here]

Objection Reply Prompt

Prospect pushed back and you don't know what to say? Use this:

Prompt
I sent a cold DM and they replied with: [paste their exact reply]

My service: [what you do]
My offer: [your price or package]

Write me one reply that:
- Acknowledges what they said without being defensive
- Keeps the conversation going without pressure
- Sounds confident, not desperate
- Is under 3 sentences
- Does not start with "I understand" or "I totally get that"
- Does not offer a discount unless I say to

Follow-Up Prompt

They haven't replied and you want to follow up without looking like you're chasing:

Prompt
I sent a cold DM [number of days] ago and got no reply. It was about: [one sentence summary]

Write me a follow-up that:
- Does not say "just checking in" or "following up on my last message"
- Brings something new, a fresh observation or a question
- Is 2 to 3 sentences
- Sounds like I thought of something new, not like I'm chasing a reply
- Keeps the door open without pressure

Platform Tone Guide

Add one of these lines to any prompt above to match where you're sending:

PlatformAdd This Line
InstagramWrite for Instagram DM, casual, warm, short
LinkedInWrite for LinkedIn, professional but human, not corporate
Twitter/XWrite for Twitter DM, punchy and direct, no fluff
WhatsAppWrite for WhatsApp, conversational, like a text from someone they know
EmailWrite for cold email, include a subject line, keep the body under 5 sentences
The best DMs sound like you spent 3 minutes on their page and typed a genuine thought. The AI handles the structure. Your real observation makes it land. Never skip the research step.

lessons.title: The Problem-Focused Approach
lessons.html:
Goal: Identify a visible gap or pain point on their page and position yourself as the expert who can solve it.

When to use: You've looked at their profile and noticed something specific like inconsistent posting, low engagement, no clear offer, weak bio, etc. This feels personal because it IS personal.
Script: Message 1

@{ handle } your work is genuinely impressive. You clearly know what you're doing and it shows.

Script: Message 2 (Send separately, right after)

But I noticed something that might be quietly costing you clients...

{ Mention the specific problem you spotted, e.g. "Your content isn't showing up consistently, which makes it hard for new people to trust you enough to reach out." OR "Your bio doesn't clearly tell people what you do or who you serve, so potential clients might be clicking away." }

I help { your niche, e.g. freelance designers, coaches, service-based business owners } fix exactly this through { what you do, e.g. a clear content strategy, optimized profile setup, and consistent posting systems } so they start attracting ready-to-buy clients without chasing anyone.

Script: Message 3 (Send separately)

Would it be okay if I shared 2 quick things you could change right now to start seeing a difference? It'll make more sense on a quick call, what's your WhatsApp?

Why This Works: You're not selling, you're noticing. Leading with a specific observation shows you actually looked at their page, which builds instant trust. Offering free tips before asking for anything makes them want to say yes.

lessons.title: Result-Oriented Approach
lessons.html:
Goal: Lead with proof. Show them what's possible by sharing a result you got for someone just like them and make them want that for themselves.

When to use: You have at least one case study, testimonial, or measurable win from a past client. Even a small result works, "helped them get 3 new clients in 30 days" is powerful.
Script: Message 1

Good morning @{ handle } I love x { mention something specific and genuine, e.g. "your brand aesthetic is clean and professional" or "you're clearly passionate about what you do" }.

Script: Message 2 (Send separately)

I recently worked with a { your niche, e.g. freelance copywriter / virtual assistant / social media manager } just like you who was struggling to { their problem, e.g. land consistent clients / get seen on Instagram / convert followers into paying customers }.

In { timeframe, e.g. 6 weeks }, we helped them { specific result, e.g. book 5 discovery calls, grow their page by 800 followers, or close their first ₦150k client }.

Script: Message 3 (Send separately)

I believe the same is possible for you and I'd love to show you exactly how. It's easier to explain on a quick call, what's your WhatsApp so I can reach you directly?

Why This Works: Results speak louder than pitches. When someone sees that you've already solved the exact problem they're facing for someone just like them, their skepticism drops. It's not "trust me", it's "here's proof."

lessons.title: Value-Based Approach
lessons.html:
Goal: Give before you ask. Lead with something genuinely useful, a resource, tip, or insight, so they associate you with value before they even know what you offer.

When to use: You're reaching out cold and want to warm them up without feeling pushy. Best used when you have a freebie, checklist, mini-guide, or helpful insight ready to send.
Script: Message 1

Good morning @{ handle } I've been following your page for a bit and I can tell you're { a genuine observation, e.g. "putting in real effort to grow" / "serious about building your brand" / "doing amazing work in the { niche } space" }.

Script: Message 2 (Send separately)

I put together a free { name of resource, e.g. "5-step Instagram growth checklist" / "Cold DM swipe file" / "Content planning guide" } specifically for { your ideal client, e.g. freelancers, coaches, service providers } who want to { what it helps them achieve, e.g. attract more clients without paid ads / land their first 3 clients online }.

Would it be okay if I sent it your way? It's completely free, just something I think would genuinely help.

Script: If They Say YES

Amazing! Here it is 👇

{ Drop the resource / link / PDF }

Let me know what you think once you've had a look. And if you want help putting any of it into practice, that's exactly what I do. What's your WhatsApp? I can walk you through how it would work for your situation.

Why This Works: Giving first removes the "what does this person want from me?" guard. When your freebie actually helps them, you've already proven your expertise before pitching anything. They come to you curious.

lessons.title: Compliment + Quick Audit Approach
lessons.html:
Goal: Open with a genuine, specific compliment to build warmth and rapport, then offer a quick audit to position yourself as the expert without being pushy.

When to use: Their page already has something going for it. You're not coming to criticize, you're coming as someone who sees their potential and knows how to unlock more of it.
Script: Message 1

Good morning @{ handle } { A specific, genuine compliment, e.g. "Your before-and-after content is so powerful, you can tell your clients genuinely love your work." OR "Your brand looks really polished, the aesthetic is cohesive and professional." } You're doing something right.

Script: Message 2 (Send separately)

That said, I noticed { 1 specific, honest thing they could improve, e.g. "your captions aren't quite pulling people in enough to comment or DM you" / "you're posting great content but it's not optimized to convert followers into actual inquiries" }.

It's a small tweak but it could make a real difference in how many people reach out to you.

Script: Message 3 (Send separately)

I'm a { your role } and I specialize in helping { your niche } { what you help them achieve }.

Can I put together a quick 3-point audit for your page, completely free? It's easier to walk you through it on a call. What's your WhatsApp?

Why This Works: People lower their guard when they feel genuinely seen and appreciated. The compliment opens the door. The honest observation earns your credibility. The free audit offer makes it almost impossible to say no.

lessons.title: The Direct Approach
lessons.html:
Goal: Be bold, clear, and confident. Skip the fluff and get straight to the point, who you are, what you do, and why you're reaching out. Busy business owners respect this.

When to use: You've identified a strong potential client and you're confident your service is exactly what they need. Great for decision-makers who don't have time for small talk.
Script: Message 1

Good evening @{ handle } I'll keep this short because I know your time is valuable.

Script: Message 2 (Send separately)

I'm { Your Name }, a freelance { your role, e.g. social media manager / copywriter / brand designer } who specializes in helping { your niche, e.g. service-based businesses, online coaches, e-commerce brands } { core result, e.g. get more clients through strategic content / build a brand that attracts premium buyers / grow their online presence without burning out }.

I looked at your page and I genuinely believe I can help you { specific opportunity you see, e.g. "turn your engagement into actual inquiries" / "create content that converts" / "position your brand to attract higher-paying clients" }.

Script: Message 3 (Send separately)

Would you be open to a quick conversation about it? What's your WhatsApp so we can link up properly.

Why This Works: Confidence is attractive. Most cold DMs are long, winding, and timid. This one respects their time, clearly states what you bring to the table, and makes a simple, low-commitment ask.

lessons.title: Soft Question-Based Opener
lessons.html:
Goal: Start a conversation with a low-pressure, curiosity-driven question that invites them to talk about their own experience, making them feel heard before you ever mention your service.

When to use: You want to qualify a lead first before pitching. This is a great opener when you're not sure if they're struggling or happy with their current situation. Let them tell you.
Script: Message 1

Good morning @{ handle } hope your week is going well. Came across your page and was genuinely impressed by { something specific, e.g. "the consistency of your content" / "your niche focus" / "the quality of your work" }.

Script: Message 2 (Send separately)

Quick question, are you currently happy with the number of clients or inquiries you're getting from your { platform, e.g. Instagram / online presence / content }?

Or do you feel like there's more potential there that hasn't been tapped yet? Either answer is totally fine, just curious.

Script: If They Say "It Could Be Better"

That's actually really common for { their type of business }, you're doing great work but the content strategy or visibility piece just isn't converting the way it should.

That's exactly what I help with. I'm a { your role } who works with { your niche } to { what you help them do }.

It'll make more sense if we speak properly. What's your WhatsApp?

Script: If They Say "Things Are Going Well"

That's great to hear. If you ever feel like you want to scale that further, feel free to reach out. Happy to support that growth when the time is right.

Why This Works: Questions make people feel involved, not sold to. By asking first, you get valuable information, and if they open up about a struggle, they've essentially just told you they need your help. You're not pitching. You're listening.

lessons.title: Niche-Expertise Opener
lessons.html:
Goal: Lead with your deep knowledge of their specific industry. Show them you get their world and that you're not just another generic freelancer, but someone who truly understands their niche inside and out.

When to use: You have real insight, experience, or results within a specific niche. This approach works best when you can speak their language and reference something that shows you know their industry deeply.
Script: Message 1

Good morning @{ handle } I specialize in working exclusively with { your niche, e.g. freelance coaches, beauty entrepreneurs, e-commerce brand owners, real estate agents } so when I came across your page, I immediately noticed a few things.

Script: Message 2 (Send separately)

Most { your niche } I talk to are dealing with the same 2-3 challenges:

→ { Challenge 1, e.g. "Posting consistently but not getting enough inquiries" }

→ { Challenge 2, e.g. "Great at what they do but struggling to communicate their value online" }

→ { Challenge 3, e.g. "No clear system to turn followers or DMs into paying clients" }

Sound familiar at all?

Script: Message 3 (Send separately)

I'm { Your Name }, a freelance { your role } and I help { your niche } solve exactly these problems through { your service }.

I've worked with { type of clients } and I know what actually moves the needle.

Would love to show you what that looks like for your business specifically. What's your WhatsApp so we can get on a quick call?

Why This Works: Specificity is the enemy of being ignored. When your DM reads like it was written for them and not copy-pasted to 100 people, they stop and pay attention. Speaking their exact language signals that you're the expert they've been looking for.

lessons.title: Not Seen
lessons.html:
📌 Situation: You sent the first DM and they never opened it. Don't panic — inboxes get crowded. Your job is to re-surface without being annoying.

Rule: Wait 2 to 3 days before following up. One follow-up only at this stage. Keep it light, curious, and human.
📩 Follow-Up Script

Good morning { Name }

Just floating this back to the top in case it got buried, inboxes can be wild!

I reached out because I genuinely think what I do could be a great fit for where you're trying to take your { business/brand/page }.

{ One-line reminder of your offer, e.g. "I help freelancers like you attract consistent clients through a simple content + DM strategy." }

Worth a quick chat? No pressure at all. 😊

Why This Works: It's warm, not desperate. You're acknowledging their busy inbox, not accusing them of ignoring you, re-stating your value in one line, and keeping the ask light.

⚠️ Key Rules:

  • Never send more than 2 follow-ups if they haven't seen the message
  • Keep a friendly tone — never guilt-trip or pressure
  • If still no response after follow-up 2, move to the After 7 Days follow-up script

lessons.title: Seen But No Response (Ghosting)
lessons.html:
📌 Situation: They opened your DM. They read it. And then... silence. No reply. This one stings but it doesn't mean it's over. It means they were interested enough to read, but something stopped them from responding. Your job is to re-open the door without making it awkward.

Rule: Wait 1–2 days after seeing the "seen" receipt, then follow up once. Be light. Be curious. Don't mention that you saw they read it , that can feel creepy.
📩 Follow-Up Script — Option A (Soft & Curious)

Good morning { Name }! 😊

Just circling back in case life got busy , totally get it!

I'd still love to share { what you offered e.g. those 3 quick tips for growing your page / that free audit / how I've been helping { your niche } get more clients }.

Even just a "not interested" is totally fine I just don't want to leave you hanging if there's something I can actually help with. 👋

📩 Follow-Up Script — Option B (Reframe with Value)

Good morning { Name }!

I know you're probably juggling a lot, so I'll keep this super short.

I help { your niche e.g. freelancers, coaches, service providers } do one thing really well: { your core result e.g. stop guessing at content and start getting actual client inquiries }.

If that's something you want, I'm here. If it's not the right time, no worries at all just let me know and I won't follow up again.

📩 Follow-Up Script — Option C (The Pattern Interrupt)

{ Name }, I'm going to be real with you for a second 😄

I don't know if my message landed weird or if life just got in the way, but I genuinely think there's something here worth a 5-minute conversation.

If I'm wrong, just say so I can handle it! But if there's even a small part of you that's curious... let's talk. 😊

💡 Why This Works:
Ghosting is usually avoidance, not rejection. These scripts remove the awkwardness, give them an easy "out" if they're not interested, and create just enough intrigue to pull them back in. Option C (pattern interrupt) works especially well because it's honest and humanizing.

lessons.title: Showed Interest Then Ghosted
lessons.html:
📌 Situation: This one hurts the most. They were IN. They replied, asked questions, seemed excited — then went completely cold. This is usually caused by: overwhelm, a budget scare, fear of commitment, or they got distracted. The key is to re-engage without making them feel guilty.

Rule: Wait 3–5 days before following up. Don't reference how excited they seemed — just re-open the conversation naturally.
📩 Script — Option A (Low-Pressure Check-In)

Hey { Name }! Hope things are going well on your end. 😊

We were in the middle of a great conversation and I just wanted to check back in — no pressure at all.

Is there anything that came up that made you hesitant? I'm genuinely happy to answer any questions or even just clarify how everything would work. Sometimes talking through the details helps. 😊

📩 Script — Option B (Re-ignite the Vision)

Hey { Name }!

I've been thinking about what you shared with me — about wanting to { their stated goal — e.g. get more clients / grow your page / build a consistent income from freelancing }.

That goal is 100% possible for you. I just want to make sure you don't let the momentum die.

Would you be open to picking up where we left off? Even just a 10-minute chat — no commitment needed. 🙏

📩 Script — Option C (Give Them an Easy Yes)

Hey { Name }! Quick one — 😊

I know timing and budget can shift, so I wanted to offer something easier to start with:

{ Describe a lower-commitment option — e.g. "Instead of the full package, we could start with a one-time strategy session so you can see how I work before anything else." }

Would that feel like a better starting point for you?

💡 Why This Works:
People ghost after showing interest because the commitment felt too big. These scripts shrink the ask, remove pressure, and reconnect them to their own goals — making it easy to say yes to something, even if it's smaller than your original offer.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

{ Name }Their first name
{ Their stated goal }What they told you they wanted to achieve

lessons.title: I Will Think About It
lessons.html:
📌 Situation: They replied with "I'll think about it." This is NOT a no. It usually means one of three things: they're unsure of the value, they're hesitant about the investment, or they just need a gentle push. Your job is to find out which one and address it with confidence, not desperation.

Rule: Never just say "okay, take your time!" that's how deals die. Acknowledge it, then dig deeper.
📩 Response Script — Option A (Curious & Warm)

Of course, { Name }! No rush at all. 😊

Can I ask ; is there anything specific you're unsure about or want more clarity on? I want to make sure you have everything you need to make the best decision for your business.

{ If they share a concern → address it directly using the relevant objection script below }

📩 Response Script — Option B (Add Urgency Without Pressure)

Totally understand, { Name }! I appreciate you being honest.

Just wanted to mention , I'm currently only taking on { number e.g. 2 } new clients this month, and I'd love for one of those spots to be yours.

If it helps, we can start small ,even a { starter offer / one-month trial / quick audit } so you can see the results before committing to anything bigger. Would that feel more comfortable? 😊

📩 Response Script — Option C (Re-anchor to Their Goal)

I hear you! Take all the time you need.

I just want to leave you with this , every week without a solid { content strategy / client pipeline / online presence } is another week of potential clients going elsewhere.

I'm not saying that to pressure you. I'm saying it because I genuinely believe you deserve to have a { page / business / brand } that works as hard as you do.

When you're ready, I'm here. And if you want to chat before then, just say the word. 🙏

💡 Why This Works:
"I'll think about it" is a soft stall. Option A uncovers the real objection. Option B creates gentle urgency. Option C reconnects them to their bigger goal. Use the one that feels most natural based on the vibe of the conversation.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

{ Name }Their first name
{ Number }Your available client slots
{ Starter offer }A lower-commitment entry point you offer
{ Content strategy / pipeline / presence }Whatever gap you're helping them fill

lessons.title: I Will Think About It (Second Time)
lessons.html:
Situation: A second version of "I'll think about it" — but this one is blank, which means it came up enough to deserve its own page. Use this when someone says it a second time, after you've already followed up once. At this point, you need to either uncover the real reason OR create enough urgency to help them decide.

Rule: This is your moment to be bold (kindly). Two "think about its" usually means something specific is holding them back. Ask directly.
📩 Response Script — Option A (Get to the Real Objection)

{ Name }, I totally respect that — and I don't want to rush you into anything. 😊

But I'd love to ask honestly: is there something specific that's making you hesitate? Whether it's the price, the timing, uncertainty about results — I'd rather know so I can actually address it instead of just leaving you hanging.

What's really going on? 🙂

📩 Response Script — Option B (Create Gentle Urgency)

Of course, { Name }! I just want to be upfront with you — I'm about to { close spots / start a new cohort / take on a new batch of clients }, so I want to make sure you don't miss out if this is something you actually want.

If you need more information to feel confident, I'm happy to jump on a quick 10-minute call — no commitment at all.

But if it's not the right fit, that's completely okay too — just let me know either way so I can plan accordingly. 🙏

📩 Response Script — Option C (Shrink the Decision)

{ Name }, what if we make this a smaller decision for now?

Instead of committing to the full thing, we could start with { mini offer — e.g. "just a 1-hour strategy session" / "a quick audit of your current setup" } — something that lets you experience the value before going all in.

Would that feel easier? 😊

💡 Why This Works:
Repeated "think about it" replies usually hide a specific fear. Option A surfaces it. Option B uses scarcity (honestly — don't fake it). Option C reduces the commitment to something almost anyone can say yes to. The goal is to move them out of indecision — gently but confidently.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

PlaceholderWhat to Write
{ Name }Their first name
{ Close spots / new cohort }Whatever urgency trigger is real for you right now
{ Mini offer }A low-risk, low-cost way to start working together

lessons.title: I Am Busy Now
lessons.html:
Situation: They told you they're busy right now. This is one of the most common deflections and it's often true! But "busy" doesn't mean "not interested." It means the timing feels off. Your job is to validate them, stay visible, and plant a seed for later.

Rule: Never push back hard on this one. Respect their time, leave the door open, and follow up at the right moment.
📩 Response Script — Option A (Validate + Stay on Their Radar)

Totally understand, { Name } sounds like you've got a lot going on! 💪

No pressure at all. I'll check back in with you in { timeframe e.g. a week or two } when things have settled.

In the meantime, feel free to save my contact I'd love to support your { business/brand/page } when the timing feels right. 😊

📩 Response Script — Option B (Plant the Seed)

That makes complete sense, { Name }! I appreciate you being upfront.

Here's a thought though , the busier you are, the more you probably need a system that works for you even when you can't. That's exactly what I build for { your niche e.g. freelancers, service providers }.

No action needed right now. But when things calm down and you're ready to stop doing everything manually I'd love to be the one to help.

📩 Response Script — Option C (Micro-Commitment Ask)

No worries at all, { Name }! 😊

Even if we can't hop on a call right now ,would it be okay if I sent you one quick tip you could use this week? Takes 2 minutes to read and might actually save you time.

No strings attached ,just something useful while you're in the thick of it.

💡 Why This Works:
Option A respects their time and keeps you top-of-mind. Option B reframes "busy" as the exact reason they need your help — without being pushy. Option C is a low-stakes way to stay connected and deliver value even before they hire you.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

PlaceholderWhat to Write
{ Name }Their first name
{ Timeframe }When you plan to follow up
{ Business/brand/page }Whatever fits their context
{ Your niche }Who you typically serve

lessons.title: I Will Reach Out When I'm Ready
lessons.html:
Situation: They've told you they'll reach out when they're ready. This is a polite way of saying "not right now" but it's NOT a door closed. The mistake most freelancers make is waiting indefinitely. Your job is to stay gently present so that when they ARE ready, you're the first person they think of.

Rule: Give them 1–2 weeks, then re-surface with value not a pitch. Don't ask "are you ready yet?" that's annoying. Lead with something useful instead.
📩 Follow-Up Script — Option A (Value-First Check-In)

Good morning{ Name }! Hope things have been going well. 😊

I came across something I thought you'd find really useful { share a tip, insight, or resource relevant to their niche/problem e.g. "a quick content hack that's been working really well for service providers right now" }.

{ Share the tip or resource in 2–3 sentences }

No agenda , just thought of you when I saw it. Let me know if you ever want to chat about how to apply it to your business!

📩 Follow-Up Script — Option B (New Month / Fresh Start Angle)

Good morning{ Name }! A new { week/month } is starting and I always think it's the best time to reset and push forward. 🙌

I know you mentioned reaching out when the time felt right , just wanted to put myself back on your radar and say the offer still stands.

If you ever want to explore what working together could look like ,even just a quick 10-minute chat I'm here and ready. 😊

📩 Follow-Up Script — Option C (Final Nudge — Keep it Clean)

Good morning{ Name }! I know you mentioned reaching out when you're ready, and I don't want to keep popping into your inbox uninvited 😄

I'll make this my last check-in for now but I just want to say, the door is always open. Whenever you're ready to { their goal e.g. start attracting more clients / build a consistent freelance income / grow your online presence }, I'd genuinely love to be a part of that.

Rooting for you either way! 🙏

💡 Why This Works:
Option A reappears with value instead of a pitch — so they're grateful, not annoyed. Option B uses a natural time anchor (new month/week) to make the follow-up feel timely. Option C is a graceful final message that leaves them feeling good about you — and ironically, often gets a reply.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

PlaceholderWhat to Write
{ Name }Their first name
{ Tip / insight / resource }Something genuinely helpful and relevant to them
{ Their goal }What they told you they wanted to achieve

lessons.title: It's Too Expensive
lessons.html:
Situation: They said it's too expensive. Before you panic or discount understand this: "too expensive" almost never means they can't afford it. It usually means they don't yet see enough value to justify the price. Your job is to shift their focus from the cost to the outcome.

Rule: Never drop your price immediately. First, validate their concern. Then reframe the investment around results.
📩 Response Script — Option A (Reframe the Investment)

I completely understand, { Name } and I appreciate you being upfront about that. 😊

Can I ask when you say it feels expensive, is it more about the total amount, or are you unsure if the results will be worth it for your specific situation?

{ Wait for their answer then respond accordingly }

Because here's the thing: if my work helps you { specific result e.g. land 3 new clients, fill your bookings for the month, or grow your audience to people who actually buy } what would that be worth to your business?

Most of my clients make back their investment within the first { timeframe e.g. 30–60 days }. I'm not just a cost I'm a growth tool.

📩 Response Script — Option B (Offer a Flexible Entry Point)

That's totally fair, { Name }, and I hear you.

Here's what I can do instead of starting with the full package, we could begin with { smaller offer e.g. a one-time strategy session / a 2-week trial / just the content audit } at { lower price or described value }.

That way you can see exactly how I work and what results look like before committing to anything bigger.

Would that feel more manageable to start? 😊

📩 Response Script — Option C (Cost of NOT Investing)

I get it and I never want anyone to feel pressured, { Name }.

But I do want you to think about this: what's the cost of not having a { content strategy / client pipeline / strong online presence } for another 3–6 months?

Lost clients, inconsistent income, hours of guessing what to post... that has a price too. It's just not one that shows up on an invoice.

I'm not the right fit for everyone but if you're serious about { their goal }, I'd love to figure out a way to make this work for you. What would feel comfortable? 🙏

💡 Why This Works:
Option A uncovers the real concern (value vs. affordability) and anchors the price to ROI. Option B removes risk with a smaller entry point. Option C reframes the conversation around the hidden cost of staying stuck. Use all three strategically based on their response.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

{ Smaller offer }A lower-risk way to start working together
{ Their goal }What they told you they want to achieve

lessons.title: I Have Someone Already
lessons.html:
Situation: They already have someone. This can feel like a dead end but it's not. It's actually a great sign. It means they already understand the value of what you do. Your job is to position yourself as complementary, better, or more specialized not as a replacement for someone they already trust.

Rule: Never trash-talk their current person. Stay respectful, stay curious, and focus on outcomes rather than comparison.
📩 Response Script — Option A (Stay Curious — Find the Gap)

Oh amazing that's great to hear, { Name }! 😊

Can I ask , are you currently happy with the results you're getting? Things like client inquiries, follower growth, or content engagement?

{ If yes → congratulate them and stay on their radar }

{ If no / "it could be better" → proceed to Option B }

📩 Response Script — Option B (Specialize vs. Replace)

That's great! Having support is so important. 😊

I ask because what I do is a bit more specialized I don't just manage pages, I specifically focus on { your niche specialization e.g. helping freelancers build a content + DM system that consistently converts followers into paying clients }.

A lot of my clients actually had someone managing their page before working with me they just wanted more focus on the { specific outcome e.g. client conversion / lead generation / niche positioning } side of things.

Is that something your current setup is covering? 🙂

📩 Response Script — Option C (Compliment + Plant Seed)

That's brilliant having a social media manager already puts you ahead of most. 🙌

I'll leave you to it then! But if you ever feel like the results could be pushed further or you want a second opinion from someone who specializes in { your niche } I'm always here.

Feel free to keep my contact. You never know when it might be useful. 😊

💡 Why This Works:
Option A asks before assuming — their current setup might not be working well. Option B differentiates you by niche rather than competing head-to-head. Option C gracefully exits while planting a seed for later. Always leave people feeling respected, never threatened.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

lessons.title: Can You Lower The Price
lessons.html:
Situation: They're interested but they want a lower price. This is actually a GOOD sign. It means they want to work with you, they just need help justifying the number. How you handle this determines whether you close at full price, find a creative middle ground, or walk away with your value intact.

Rule: Never immediately say yes to a discount. It signals that your original price wasn't real and it trains clients to always negotiate. Always anchor the value first.
📩 Response Script — Option A (Hold Your Price — Anchor to Value)

I really appreciate you asking, { Name } and I want to be upfront with you. 😊

My pricing is based on the results I deliver and the time I invest in each client. It's not something I can reduce without reducing the quality of what I provide.

What I CAN tell you is this: the clients who invest in { your service } typically see { specific result e.g. their first 3 clients within 30 days / a 40% increase in inquiries / consistent monthly income from their skills } which makes the investment feel very different when you're on the other side of it.

Is there a specific part of the package you're unsure about? Sometimes we can restructure things without lowering the price. 🙏

📩 Response Script — Option B (Offer an Alternative — Not a Discount)

I hear you, { Name }! I don't typically lower my rates but here's what I CAN do:

Instead of the full package, we could start with { a smaller version of your offer e.g. "just the content strategy piece" / "a 2-week intensive" / "a single audit session" } at { a lower price point }.

That way you're investing less upfront, getting real value, and can decide if you want to continue from there.

Does that work? 😊

📩 Response Script — Option C (Payment Plan Offer)

I understand, { Name } budgets are real and I respect that.

One thing I can offer is a payment plan instead of paying { full price } upfront, you could pay { split amount e.g. ₦X now and ₦X at the end of the first month }.

That way you're getting the full service and the full results, just spread out in a way that feels more manageable. Would that help? 🙏

📩 Response Script — Option D (Graceful No-Discount Stand)

I totally get it, { Name }, and I appreciate you being honest with me.

Here's the thing I've set my prices intentionally based on the value I deliver, and lowering them isn't something I'm able to do right now.

But I'd hate for price to be the only thing standing between you and { the result they want }. If you'd like, we can explore a different package or entry point that fits your budget better.

What would feel comfortable for you to start with? 😊

💡 Why This Works:
Option A holds the price and anchors it to ROI the strongest position. Option B reframes it as a scope change (not a discount). Option C introduces a payment plan — often the real barrier is cash flow, not price. Option D is firm but kind — it respects you both.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

{ Your service }What you offer

lessons.title: Unexpected Reply: Conversation Recovery Scripts
lessons.html:
They replied but their message doesn't fit any of the 10 objection scripts. Maybe it's vague, maybe it's off-topic, maybe it's just one word. This page covers the 6 most common off-script situations with a word-for-word reply for each one.

One Word Reply

What they sent: "Interesting" / "Ok" / "Hmm" / "Tell me more"

This is a warm signal. They are curious but not open yet. Do not pitch. Ask one question to open the door wider.

Your reply:

"Haha glad it caught your attention. Quick question, is [the problem you mentioned] something you're actually dealing with right now or more of a back-burner thing?"

Why this works: it qualifies their interest without pressure. If they say back-burner you have a reason to follow up later. If they say yes, the conversation is open.

They Ask to See Your Work

What they sent: "Can I see some of your work?" / "Do you have examples?" / "What have you done before?"

This is one of the best replies you can get. Don't just drop a link. Ask one quick question so you send the most relevant stuff.

Your reply:

"Yep, happy to share. Just so I send you the most relevant stuff, are you looking for examples in [their niche] or general [your service type] work?"

Why this works: it shows you have range and makes them feel like they're getting something tailored. It also tells you exactly how to position your portfolio.

They Ask Your Price Right Away

What they sent: "How much do you charge?" / "What are your rates?"

Giving a number too soon gets you dismissed before any value is established.

Your reply:

"Depends on what you actually need. I do a few different things and pricing reflects that. What's the main thing you're trying to fix right now?"

Why this works: it moves the conversation toward their problem before you name a number. By the time price comes up, value is already in the room.

They Question Your Credibility

What they sent: "How long have you been doing this?" / "Who have you worked with?" / "Are you legit?"

This is not skepticism. This is buying behaviour. They're checking you out before saying yes.

Your reply:

"[Honest answer about your experience]. Most recently I worked with [type of client] on [specific outcome]. Happy to share more on a call if it's helpful. What does your situation look like right now?"

Why this works: it answers their question with proof then brings the conversation back to them. Never end on a credential.

They Replied Positively Then Disappeared

What they sent: "This looks great!" / "I'd definitely be interested", then nothing for 3 days

Do not follow up with "just checking in." They said they were interested. They got distracted. Treat it like a warm lead, not a rejection.

Your reply (3 days later):

"Hey [name], I was thinking about what you mentioned about [their specific situation] and had one more thought on it. Would it make sense to get on a 15-minute call this week to talk through it properly?"

Why this works: it references the real conversation, makes them feel remembered, and offers a low-commitment next step.

They Reply With Something Completely Off-Topic

What they sent: A question about something unrelated / a joke / a meme

This usually means they're comfortable with you. Don't ignore it and don't force the redirect awkwardly.

Your reply:

"[Acknowledge it in one sentence]. Anyway, circling back to what I sent, is [the core problem you raised] something that's on your radar right now?"

Why this works: meeting their off-topic message briefly shows you're human. Then you redirect cleanly without making it weird.

The rule for all unexpected replies: one question, focused on their situation, always moves things forward.

lessons.title: Follow-Up Strategies
lessons.html:
The follow-up is where most freelancers give up and where the real money is made. Most clients don't say yes on the first message. Most deals close on the 2nd, 3rd, or even 5th touch. Your follow-up game is your income game.

Use this page as your master reference every time you're about to reach out again.

🗓️ The Follow-Up Timeline

TouchpointWhen to SendGoal
Message 1Day 0Open the conversation
Follow-Up 1Day 2Re-surface, stay warm
Follow-Up 2Day 5Change the angle, add value
Follow-Up 3Day 7Graceful exit, leave the door open
Follow-Up 4After 1 MonthFresh start, re-engage with new hook
⚠️ Never send more than 3 follow-ups in the first 7 days. After that, give it a full month before reaching out again. Respecting their space is what keeps you from being blocked — and keeps the door open.

🧠 The Golden Rules of Following Up

1. Never repeat the same message twice.

If it didn't work once, it won't work again. Change your angle lead with a tip, a result, a question, or a pattern interrupt.

2. Always lead with value, not desperation.

Every follow-up should make them feel like connecting with you is worth their time not like you're chasing them for a sale.

3. Keep it short.

Follow-up messages should be shorter than your original DM. Two to four sentences max. Busy people skim. Make it easy to read and respond to.

4. One clear ask per message.

Don't ask three questions or pitch multiple things. Pick one "Would you be open to a quick chat?" and stop there.

5. Match the energy.

If they seemed warm before going cold → stay warm. If they were brief → be brief. Mirror their communication style, not your anxiety.

6. Always leave the door open.

Even when you're sending a final message, make sure they feel like reaching out to you later is still a comfortable option. No guilt. No pressure. No "this is your last chance."

📲 Daily Outreach System

HabitTarget
New cold DMs sent per day15–25 personalized messages
Follow-ups sent per day10–15 across your pipeline
Profile engagements before DMingLike + comment on 1–2 recent posts first
Tracking methodSpreadsheet, Notion board, or CRM
💡 Pro tip: Engage with their content (like, comment, share a genuine reaction) 24–48 hours before sending a cold DM. When your name already feels familiar, your DM gets opened faster and responded to more.

🔁 What to Track for Each Lead

For every person you DM, note:

  • Date of first message
  • Date of each follow-up
  • Their response status (No reply / Seen / Replied / Interested / Ghosted after interest)
  • Next follow-up date
  • Notes (what they said, what objection came up, what you offered)
This turns your DMs from random shots in the dark into a real client pipeline. You'll know exactly who to follow up with, when, and how.

⚡ Quick Mindset Reminder

No reply is not a rejection. It's just not a yes yet.

People are busy. Inboxes are full. Life gets in the way. Your job is to stay visible, stay valuable, and stay patient — because the freelancer who follows up consistently and professionally is the one who closes the deal.

Keep going. The next yes is closer than you think. 🙏

lessons.title: After 2 Days
lessons.html:
Situation: You sent your first DM 2 days ago and heard nothing. They may not have seen it, they might have seen it and gotten distracted, or life simply got in the way. This is your first follow-up —keep it warm, breezy, and value-forward. No guilt. No pressure.

Rule: One follow-up at this stage. Short, friendly, and focused on them — not on you needing a reply.
📩 Script — Option A (Light & Curious)

Good morning{ Name }! 👋

Just bumping this up in case it got lost in the noise inboxes can be wild 😄

I reached out because I genuinely think there's something here worth a quick conversation. I help { your niche e.g. freelancers, coaches, service providers } { core result e.g. attract consistent clients through content + smart outreach } and from what I've seen of your page, I think you'd be a great fit.

Would love to connect if you're open to it! 😊

📩 Script — Option B (Lead with a Tip)

Hey { Name }! 👋

I sent you a message a couple of days ago and just wanted to follow up — no pressure at all!

While I'm here, I wanted to share something quick that's been working really well for { your niche } right now:

{ Quick, genuinely useful tip e.g. "Posting 3–4x a week with a clear CTA in every caption can double your DM inquiries within 2–3 weeks." }

Something to try even before we chat! And if you'd like more tailored strategies for your page specifically I'm here. 😊

💡 Why This Works:
Option A is clean and low-pressure it re-surfaces without being needy. Option B delivers instant value before asking for anything, which makes them feel like connecting with you is already worth it.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

PlaceholderWhat to Write
{ Name }Their first name or handle
{ Your niche }Who you serve
{ Core result }What you help clients achieve
{ Quick tip }A genuinely useful, niche-specific insight

lessons.title: After 5 Days
lessons.html:
Situation: Still no reply after 5 days. They've had enough time to see your messages which means either life is genuinely hectic, or they're on the fence. At this point, change your angle slightly. Don't repeat the same message. Come back with a different hook a fresh perspective, a new piece of value, or a softer ask that's harder to ignore.

Rule: Never copy-paste your first two messages. If the same thing hasn't worked twice, try a different angle. Curiosity beats repetition every time.
📩 Script — Option A (Reframe with a Question)

Good morning{ Name }! 😊

I know you're probably juggling a lot I'll keep this short.

Quick question: is growing your { business/client base/online presence } something that's on your radar right now, or is your focus somewhere else entirely?

Either answer is genuinely helpful for me to know no sales pitch, just curious. 🙂

📩 Script — Option B (Share a Win / Social Proof)

Good morning{ Name }! 👋

Just wanted to share something exciting I recently helped a { type of client similar to them e.g. freelance designer / virtual assistant / social media manager } { specific result e.g. land their first 3 paying clients in 3 weeks / grow from 200 to 1,500 engaged followers / close a ₦200k project through a cold DM }.

It got me thinking about you and what's possible for your { page / business / brand } with the right strategy.

Still happy to share what we did would that be useful? 😊

📩 Script — Option C (The Honest Check-In)

Good morning{ Name }, I'm going to keep it real with you 😄

I've followed up a couple of times and haven't heard back, which is completely fine! I just don't want to keep popping up if it's not something you're interested in.

If now isn't the right time no worries at all, just say the word and I'll stop following up. But if there's even a small part of you that's curious about { what you offer e.g. building a content system that brings in clients on autopilot }... I'd genuinely love to have that conversation. 🙏

💡 Why This Works:
At 5 days, you need to earn their attention again — not demand it. Option A uses a low-stakes question to restart the conversation. Option B re-ignites interest with social proof. Option C is refreshingly honest and often gets a reply simply because it's unexpected.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

PlaceholderWhat to Write
{ Name }Their first name or handle
{ Business / client base / online presence }What fits their context
{ Type of client }Someone similar to the person you're messaging
{ Specific result }A real, measurable win from a past client
{ What you offer }Your core service in plain language

lessons.title: After 7 Days
lessons.html:
Situation: Seven days in. No reply across multiple touch points. This is your closing message in the first follow-up sequence make it count. The goal here is to leave the door WIDE open while removing all pressure. A well-written final follow-up often gets a reply simply because it feels final — and people don't want to miss out.

Rule: This is not a "last chance" threat. It's a graceful exit that keeps your reputation intact and the relationship warm. Leave them feeling respected not chased.
📩 Script — Option A (The Graceful Exit)

Good evening{ Name }! 👋

I've reached out a few times now and I don't want to keep filling up your inbox I genuinely respect your time😊

I'll make this my last message for a while. If growing your { business / page / client pipeline } becomes a priority down the road, I'd love to be the one to help you get there.

Feel free to save my contact the door is always open. Wishing you nothing but growth!

📩 Script — Option B (Leave with Value)

Good morning { Name }!

Last message from me for now I promise 😄

Before I go, I wanted to leave you with something useful:

{ A genuinely valuable tip, insight, or resource e.g. "The #1 thing that helps freelancers land clients faster: a pinned post that clearly states what you do, who you help, and how to work with you. Most people skip this and lose leads daily." }

Hope that helps regardless of whether we work together. If you ever want a full strategy session, I'm just a DM away. 😊

Take care!

📩 Script — Option C (The Curiosity Closer)

Hey { Name }, last one I promise this isn't a guilt trip 😄

I just want to say: whatever is going on behind the scenes for you right now, I hope it's going well.

If you're ever in a season where { the pain point e.g. getting more clients consistently / building a freelance income that doesn't feel like a guessing game / growing your online presence without burning out } becomes the priority come find me.

I'll be here. 🙏 Rooting for you either way!

💡 Why This Works:
A graceful goodbye creates psychological safety — they stop feeling chased, and ironically, that's when many people reply. Option B leaves a lasting impression by adding value on your way out. Option C is warm, human, and memorable — it keeps you top of mind without any pressure.

✏️ Fill-in Guide:

PlaceholderWhat to Write
{ Name }Their first name or handle
{ Business / page / client pipeline }Whatever fits their context
{ Valuable tip }A specific, niche-relevant insight you can leave them with
{ The pain point }The core challenge you help solve

lessons.title: After A Month
lessons.html:
Situation: A full month has passed. They went cold, you gave them space now you're back. This isn't desperate, it's strategic. A lot can change in 30 days: their budget shifts, their business grows, their current solution stops working, or they finally feel ready. One final, well-timed message can unlock a conversation that wasn't possible before.

Rule: Don't reference all your previous messages. Start fresh. Make it feel like a natural check-in, not a final attempt at a sale. Lead with relevance — something timely, something new, or something that reminds them of their goal.
📩 Script — Option A (The Fresh Start)

Good morning{ Name }! 👋

It's been a little while since I reached out hope things have been going well on your end! 😊

💡 Why This Works:
A month is long enough for their situation to have changed — and for them to have forgotten the awkwardness of not replying. Option A is a clean, no-baggage reset. Option B uses the energy of a new month as a natural hook. Option C reactivates their curiosity with fresh social proof that mirrors their own situation.

lessons.title: Post-Proposal Follow-Up: 3 Messages That Reopen Dead Deals
lessons.html:
You sent the proposal. They read it. And then nothing.

Most proposals don't get rejected. They get forgotten. These three messages bring you back into the conversation without making you look like you're chasing.

Before You Use These

Never follow up by saying "just wanted to check if you've had a chance to review." That message tells them you're waiting. It shifts all the power to them.

Every message below comes from a place of value, not need.

Follow-Up 1: 48 Hours After Sending

When to use it: You sent the proposal and heard nothing.

Message:

"Good morning[name], sent over the details yesterday. I was thinking about what you mentioned on our call about [specific thing they said] and wanted to add one thing I think makes this more relevant to your situation. [Add one specific point based on what you learned on the call.] Let me know if that changes anything or if you have questions."

Why this works: it doesn't remind them you're waiting. It shows you're still thinking about their problem. The added point gives them a reason to open the proposal again without pressure.

Follow-Up 2: 5 Days After Sending

When to use it: Still no response after the first follow-up.

Message:

"Good morning[name], I know things get busy. Just wanted to flag that the pricing in the proposal is available until [specific date]. After that I'll need to reassess based on my current workload. If the timing doesn't work, no pressure at all, just wanted to be transparent."

Why this works: your time genuinely fills up. This is not a manipulation tactic. It creates a soft deadline without ultimatums and gives them an easy out if they're not interested.

Follow-Up 3: 10 Days After Sending

When to use it: Two follow-ups and still nothing. This is the last one.

Message:

"Good morning[name], I'm going to close out this proposal on my end and free up the spot. If the timing works out in the future feel free to reach back out, happy to revisit. Hope things are going well."

Why this works: it removes the offer, which creates real urgency. It leaves the door open without begging. About 30% of proposals that looked dead come back after this message.

If They Reply After Any of These

They're still interested but need more time:

"No problem. What's the realistic timeline on your end? I'll hold the spot if I can."

They went with someone else:

"Got it, totally fine. Out of curiosity, was there something about the proposal that didn't quite fit? Always useful to know."

They're no longer interested:

"Appreciate you letting me know. If anything changes, you know where to find me."

Three follow-ups maximum on any proposal. After three, move on. Your pipeline should never depend on one person saying yes.

lessons.title: Discovery Call Script: From Call to Closed Client
lessons.html:
You got their WhatsApp number. Now what?

This page gives you the exact structure for a 15-minute WhatsApp call that moves naturally from hello to closed client. No pitch deck needed. No pressure. Just the right questions in the right order.

The goal of the call is simple: understand their situation well enough that your service becomes the obvious next step.

The Structure

Four parts. Fifteen minutes. One clear next step at the end.

Part 1: Open (2 minutes)

Start warm. You already have their WhatsApp so the barrier is lower. Don't open by pitching.

Say this:

"Good morning[name], good to finally speak. So from our DMs I got a rough idea of what's going on but I'd rather hear it from you directly. What's actually happening with [the problem you spotted] right now?"

This shows you paid attention. It also lets them speak first, which is where you want them.

Part 2: Diagnose (7 minutes)

Ask these four questions in this order. Their answers are your close.

Question 1: Understand the problem

"How long has this been going on?"

Question 2: Understand what they've already tried

"What have you already tried to fix it?"

Question 3: Make the cost real

"What's it costing you right now, in time, money, or missed clients, to have this still unresolved?"

Question 4: Get their vision

"If we fixed this completely, what does that actually look like for you 3 months from now?"

Take notes. Their exact words from questions 3 and 4 become your close.

Part 3: Position (4 minutes)

Do not present a full proposal. Draw a direct line from their problem to your solution using their own words.

Say this:

"Based on what you've told me, here is what I think is happening and what I'd do about it."

[Explain your solution in 3 to 4 sentences using the language they used on the call.]

"The way I work is [brief explanation of your process]. Most clients see [specific outcome] within [realistic timeframe]. Does that sound like what you're looking for?"

Part 4: Close (2 minutes)

If they said yes to Part 3, move to logistics immediately.

If they're ready:

"The way we'd get started is [your first step]. I can send you the details by tomorrow. Does that work?"

If they need to think:

"Totally fine. What specifically do you need to think through? I'd rather address it now while we're both here than leave you with an open question."

If they bring up budget:

"What's the number that works for you? Let's see if there's a version of this that makes sense."

The 24-Hour Follow-Up

If they did not commit on the call, send this on WhatsApp within 24 hours.

"Good morning[name], really good speaking earlier. Based on what you told me about [their problem], I've put together a quick summary of what I'd do and what working together looks like. [Send your offer or a voice note walking through it.] Let me know if you have any questions."

What Not to Do on a Call

  • Do not talk more than 40% of the time
  • Do not show your portfolio unless they specifically ask
  • Do not apologise for your price
  • Do not use the words "cheap" or "affordable" to describe your service
  • Do not end the call without a clear next step both of you agreed on
The person who asks the most questions controls the call. Ask, listen, reflect their words back, then present. That sequence closes more than any pitch.

lessons.title: Outreach Audit: Diagnose Why Your DMs Aren't Working
lessons.html:
If your DMs are not getting replies, the problem is in one of three places: the message, the prospect, or the volume. This page helps you figure out which one in under 10 minutes.

Track Your Numbers Weekly

You cannot fix what you don't measure. After every week, record these four numbers:

MetricYour NumberTarget
DMs sent10 to 20 per day
Replies received50 to 70%
Conversations that moved to a call or proposal20 to 30% of replies
Clients closed1 to 3 per 50 DMs

If any number is well below the target, run the diagnostic below.

Reply Rate Below 20%

The problem is almost always the opener. Work through this:

  • Is my compliment about something specific I observed, or is it generic?
  • Does my first sentence mention them and not me?
  • Am I opening with an observation or question, not an introduction?
  • Is my message under 4 sentences?
  • Am I reaching out to the right accounts, real businesses with an audience and a relevant niche?

Fix: rewrite your opener using the Compliment + Audit or Soft Question script and test for 3 days.

Reply Rate Is Fine But Conversations Stall

The problem is what happens after the first reply. Work through this:

  • Am I pitching before they've shown interest in the solution?
  • Am I asking for a call before enough context is established?
  • Am I sending one-line replies instead of advancing the conversation?
  • When they go quiet, am I following up with something new or just checking in?

Fix: use the Unexpected Reply: Conversation Recovery Scripts page and the follow-up sequence.

Conversations Happen But You're Not Closing

The problem is the offer or the call. Work through this:

  • Is my offer tied to a specific outcome they care about?
  • Am I presenting price before value is established?
  • Am I handling objections or just accepting them?
  • Am I following up after the call with a clear next step?

Fix: use the Discovery Call Script and the Post-Proposal Follow-Up pages.

Closing But Getting Low-Quality or Low-Paying Clients

The problem is targeting. Work through this:

  • Are the accounts I'm reaching out to big enough to have a real budget?
  • Am I leading with outcomes or selling tasks?
  • Is my offer framed around the result I deliver, not the hours I put in?

Fix: revisit the Crafting Your Grand Slam Offer page and How to Find 20 Ideal Prospects in 20 Minutes.

Weekly Review: 5 Questions Every Friday

  1. How many DMs did I send this week?
  2. What was my reply rate?
  3. Which script angle performed best?
  4. What objection came up most and how did I handle it?
  5. What one thing would I change next week?
When to Switch Scripts

If you've sent a specific script to 30 or more relevant prospects and your reply rate is consistently under 15%, switch angles. Not because the script is bad but because your audience at this moment responds better to a different approach. You have 7 angles. Use them.

Cold outreach is a system, not a single event. One bad week tells you nothing. Two weeks of consistent tracking tells you exactly what to fix.

lessons.title: Instagram Guidelines & Limits
lessons.html:
If you’re sliding into DMs to land clients, you need to play it smart.
Instagram loves authentic connection and hates spammy behavior.

Here’s what you need to know:

Daily DM Limits

  • New accounts (under 3 months):
    Stay under 20–25 new DMs/day
    Spread them out over the day — don’t batch spam
  • Established accounts:
    You can usually send 50–80 DMs/day safely
    But again: pace yourself. No more than 10 DMs per hour.

Tip: Don’t copy-paste the same message 50 times. IG detects that as spam.

Avoid Getting Flagged or Blocked

Instagram may block your DM function if you:

  • Send too many messages too fast
  • Use too many links or emojis
  • Repeatedly message people who don’t follow you
  • Send “salesy” messages to people with no context

👎 Doing this too often can lead to:

  • DM restrictions
  • Shadowbans (where your content doesn’t reach anyone)
  • Temporary account blocks
  • Even permanent bans for repeat offenders

Best Practices for Safe & Effective DMs

  • Personalize every message (mention their name, niche, or recent content)
  • Space out messages (5–10 minutes apart is great)
  • Use voice notes or short video messages for variety
  • Don’t drop links in the first message — build connection first
  • Avoid spammy words like “guarantee,” “promo,” “offer ends,” or “buy now”

Pro Tip: Build a warm-up system. Engage with their posts for 1–2 days before DMing. You’ll get better replies + stay under the radar.

Instagram Community Guidelines (Quick Reminder)

Instagram wants conversations that are:

  • Respectful
  • Authentic
  • Helpful (not pushy)
  • Non-automated (avoid bots + mass DM tools)

Breaking the rules = getting limited, no matter how good your offer is.

Extra tip

Treat DMs like you’re texting a new friend not pitching a stranger.

Instagram rewards real connection.

And if you follow the rules above, you can stay in IG’s good books and turn DMs into $$$.

lessons.title: Secret Cold DM Strategies
lessons.html:
Here are some proven strategies to increase the chances of your cold DMs and emails being seen and opened:

1. Personalization is important

💡

If you don’t make it feel personal, they won’t even read it.


✅ Use their name or brand name

✅ Mention a specific product, reel, or post

✅ Show that you’re familiar with their content or niche

Always customize the DM to show that you've researched their profile. Mention something specific about their business or Instagram page (e.g., "I love how you offer natural skincare solutions," or "Your treatments look amazing!")


Example:“Hey [brand name], I saw your recent post on { mention a post } your approach is so refreshing. I had an idea that could help boost its reach.

2.Hook in the First Line

💡

The first line is what shows in DM previews ,treat it like a headline.


Use curiosity, bold opinions, pain points, or value teasers.


Winning Hook Examples:


“Can I show you how to turn one reel into 7 days of content?”


“You’re killing it… but your content deserves way more reach”


“Most {your target audience e.g clothing brands } make this mistake, do you?”

3. Keep It Conversational (Not Robotic)

💡

You’re not pitching, you’re starting a conversation.Talk like a real person — casual but helpful.


✅ Be warm, clear, and human

✅ Avoid formal, “salesy” vibes


Example:“I work with { target audience e g, skincare brands} to help them turn Reels into actual sales. I had a quick strategy idea that could work for your brand ,would you be open to hear it?”

4. Use the “Value Tease” Formula

💡

Don't drop your whole offer. Tease the value, then ask if they want to know more.

Formula: Who you help + what result you get + curious CTA


Example:“I help { your target audience e.g skincare brands} grow on IG with viral Reels . One of my recent clients got 3x engagement in 2 weeks. Want me to send you the strategy?”

5. Follow Up (Most Replies Come Here!)

💡

People are busy. They often need 1–2 nudges.

✅ Follow up after 2–3 days

✅ Be polite, reaffirm value

✅ Don’t guilt-trip — make it casual

Follow-up example:“Good morning, just circling back in case you missed this! Let me know if you’d like me to send over that scial media hack I mentioned it’s working crazy well for skincare brands right now

6. Your Profile Sells You First

💡

After they open your DM, they check your profile.So before you start outreach, optimize your Instagram bio to answer:


Who do you help?
What do you do for them?
Where’s the proof or next step?

Include:


A highlight of past results/testimonials
A pinned Reel or carousel with proof/tips
Clear, niche-specific bio (Ex: “SMM for skincare brands | I help you sellout your products and grow on IG)

Include a Call-to-Action (CTA)

  • End your DM with a clear next step. For example:
    • “Would you like me to show you a quick strategy to boost your Instagram bookings? Let me know, I’d love to help!”
    • “If you’re interested in a quick chat about your goals, I’d be happy to share some tips!

Be Consistent:

Don’t be discouraged by no responses. People are busy, and it might take 2-3 touches before they engage. Ensure your follow-up message is short and polite, not pushy.

For Email Outreach:

Craft a Catchy Subject Line:

  • Your subject line is the first thing they see, so make it stand out. Keep it short, clear, and curiosity-driven.
    • “Can I Help You Get More Clients on Instagram?”
    • “Your Competitors Are Already Doing This – Let’s Talk”
    • “What If You Could Add 10+ Clients in a Week?”

Start With a Strong Introduction:

The first sentence intriguing to hook them. Examples:

  • “I came across your profile and noticed your spa has so much potential to grow on Instagram.”
  • “I see you’re already doing great work in the esthetician space, and I have an idea to help you get even more clients.

Make It About Them, Not You:

  • Frame the email as a value proposition for them. Show how your service can solve their problems or make their life easier.
    • Instead of: “I offer social media management,” say “Here’s a way to get more clients without spending hours on social media

Keep It Short and Scannable:

  • Busy professionals don’t have time for long emails. Get straight to the point, and use bullet points to break up the content.

Personalize the Email:

  • Mention something specific about their business (e.g., “I saw your spa offers luxurious facials” or “I love your commitment to all-natural skincare”)

Create Curiosity with Results and Testimonials:

  • Drop a statistic or result early on to create intrigue: “I helped a client grow their Instagram reach from 3k to 89k in just 3 months, and here’s how we did it…

Offer a Clear Call to Action:

  • Make it easy for them to take the next step:
    • “Are you available for a quick 10-minute call this week to chat about how I can help you grow your social media?”
    • “If you’re interested in hearing more, just reply with ‘yes,’ and I’ll schedule a time that works for you.

Follow Up (Without Being Pushy):

  • Send a follow-up email if you haven’t received a response after 3-4 days. Keep it friendly and provide additional value or insights.

General Tips for Both:

  1. Use a Professional Profile:
    • Ensure your Instagram profile and email signature are polished, showcasing your services and previous work. Your profile should look like a trusted expert, not a random person.
  2. Timing is Everything:
    • Send your cold DMs and emails during optimal hours. Try mornings (9-11 AM) or late afternoons (2-4 PM) to increase the likelihood of your messages being opened.
  3. Leverage Social Proof:
    • Include client testimonials, before-and-after results, or examples of your work in your messages. This builds trust and credibility.
  4. Be Brief, Be Bold, and Be Polite:
    • Avoid overly long messages. Stick to concise and engaging language that respects their time. Use a confident yet friendly tone, showing that you know what you’re talking about.
  5. Don’t Over Send (Quality over Quantity):
    • Sending too many cold DMs or emails can come off as spammy. Focus on targeting the right clients and making each outreach personal, thoughtful, and relevant.
